In addition to these, there will be three members drawn from the civil service and three members drawn from the citizens of Canada. I might say tentatively that possibly one might be from the press, one from the radio and one from the schools or colleges or other educational institutions. But that is merely by the way; that has not been definitely decided.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: To act with or without pay?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: None of these men will receive any pay. Their expenses of course will be provided for, such expenses as may be necessary for their travelling and any work they have to do, but they will not be in receipt of any salary or honorarium of any kind. There is also provision for an executive officer of the board, who is designated in the bill as a commissioner. He will be the only paid official. It will be his duty to act under the instruction or supervision of the board in its practical work of coordination and that sort of thing.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Is he to be a member of the board?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: No.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Who, then, is the eighth member?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: There are to be two members of the government, three from the civil service and three from outside.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Who is to be the second member of the government? The minister mentioned the Minister of Trade and Commerce as one; perhaps the Minister of Agriculture will be the other?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
Well, that might be quite
all right; they seem to work together pretty well. I did think my hon. friend was serious in his question, but I see he was not.
I have spoken then of the composition of the board, providing for a commissioner who will be the executive officer of the board. In addition, there will be an interdepartmental committee. It might not be necessary to include that in the bill, but it is thought well to give that committee an official standing. The members of that committee will be drawn from the departments which have film activities, the chairman to be the commissioner himself. Then, of course, we have the

government film bureau which is operating under the Department of Trade and Commerce. I may say in passing that according to those who know, the film bureau which we have now, is as well equipped in its rather small way as any such plant in north America. It is, of course, the intention that the films which will be made for the government shall as far as possible be produced in the government film bureau now in the Department of Trade and Commerce. That, however, is not obligatory; it may be found that a department or a minister may wish to have a certain kind of film produced which could better be prepared by some private organization, and if he receives the approval of the film board that may be done.
I should perhaps add, because there seems to have been a certain amount of uneasiness in regard to this, that the bill does not provide in any way for supervision or control of private film organizations. The primary and really the only purpose of the bill is to provide for improvement and efficiency in the preparation of government films, whether prepared by the bureau or by outside film concerns.
The purpose is to provide also for efficiency in distribution. There is room for a great deal of improvement in the economic and efficient distribution of these films, both in Canada and more particularly abroad, where Canada is being advertised in so many ways.
I may add, in conclusion, that this board is not being established with the intention of providing jobs for anybody. There is really to be only one paid man in the organization.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
How much will he be
paid?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
That is not set out in the
bill. It is provided that the governor in council shall make the appointment.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
He might be taken out
of the civil service.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: He might, conceivably.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
He is more likely to be
taken out of the house.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
That would be out of the
service too.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
Is the
hon. member an applicant?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
That has not been considered. But the only other paid official might be a clerk or a stenographer. It is not a board or organization that is going to require the expenditure of a great deal of public money. The purpose is simply to coordinate what we

National Film Board
are doing now, to make it more efficient, perhaps less expensive, and to see that the distribution of films is done to better advantage.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
Will the minister promise
that this board will not be built up into a large new department?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: I will promise it as far as I am concerned.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
It is a hard thing to stop
once it starts.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
The minister has suggested that parliament should look to the future and be thinking of national films. As I read the reports of the Department of Trade and Commerce, the films that we are producing at the present time are used largely for promotion of trade and of our tourist business. I suggest to him that provision should be made now for making and distributing national films, designed to help Canadians in all parts of Canada to understand the ways of living and the problems of Canadians in other parts. Perhaps every hon. member must have been impressed by two facts:	first, that it is
difficult for Canadians in one part of Canada to understand what is going on in other parts of the countiy, and, second, that moving pictures are having a remarkable effect on the Canadian people, particularly on the children and young men and women.
I see by "Canada 1939," issued by the Department of Trade and Commerce, that the motion picture continues to be the most popular form of amusement in this dominion. Figures for 1937 show 1,047 motion picture theatres, with a total of 134,374,061 paid admissions. We all know how the children flock to the moving picture theatres on Saturdays and other holidays and, in fact, on every occasion; I would ask the minister whether there is not some chance of this national film board, some time within not the distant but the near future, making and distributing films showing Canadian life, and making arrangements with the moving picture theatres across Canada to show these pictures once they are made.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
Perhaps I have not made myself quite as clear as I had hoped. One of the purposes we have in mind in establishing the film board is the very one mentioned by my hon. friend, the making of a national film along national or perhaps instructive lines, or even by way of amusement, if you like, but for the general cultural development of the children of this country. That, I think the committee would admit, is hardly possible while the film activities remain under the control of more than one department. Cast your mind now over the various depart-71492-105
ments of government which issue films. Is any one of them qualified, or is it the duty of any one department, to prepare, issue or distribute a film along national lines? I would say not, and that is one of the reasons for the establishment of this board, which not only can concern itself with reviewing and passing upon requests for films coming from the various departments but can of itself, as the funds become available-which of course must be voted by parliament-initiate films of the national character referred to by my hon. friends.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Will it be possible to make arrangements with moving picture theatres to show these films once they are made?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Quite so; that is one of the things in which perhaps we have not been as efficient as we could have been. These films should have been distributed much more widely than has been the case in the past, and we think that by the creation of this board that purpose will be much better served than formerly.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: The theatres will use them?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: I think that is quite probable.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: The minister stated a moment ago that there were various government departments at present engaged in making films of various kinds. I wonder if the creation of this board and the consolidation of this work will lead to the displacement of any considerable number of workers at present engaged in that line of activity?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: I think not. As a matter of fact, if we concentrate the work in our own film bureau in the Department of Trade and Commerce, it will give employment to people there. In the past, for instance, if one department has had its films prepared by some private organization, that work will be transferred to our own bureau, so where work ceases in one place it will begin in another. I do not think there will be any net reduction in employment.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
Then I take it from the remarks of the minister that this will not affect any large number of jobs. My next question is, what cooperation, if any, will there be between this new board and the various extension departments of the universities throughout Canada? I understand many universities make films of this kind, and I should like to know if it is the intention that this film board will cooperate with those extension departments in order to prepare films on various subjects which might be to the general advantage of the people of Canada.

National Film Board

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: The primary purpose of the bill is to coordinate government activities. Beyond that certainly there will be plenty of scope for the board itself to cooperate with any other interest, whether it be a university, a theatre, or anyone concerned in the dissemination of information and general publicity for Canada. I am afraid I cannot go so far as to say that at the moment any definite arrangement is contemplated to cooperate with the universities. That is all in the future, but I think it is quite within the compass of the activities of the board and quite within the bounds of expectation as to what the board may accomplish.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: I am glad to hear the minister make that statement, and I believe this will fill a long felt want in the country. My last question is this: We now have a board controlling broadcasting and another controlling the marketing of our wheat. I should like to know if this new board will be responsible to parliament. Apparently the other boards are not responsible to parliament, and their work may be, if not criticized, at least discussed in this house at certain times. I think in connection with an educational matter of this kind we should have an opportunity of discussing these questions from time to time. For that reason I am wondering if this board will be responsible to this parliament.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Any work done by the board on its own initiative, for instance in preparing a national film, would necessitate the expenditure of money. That money must be voted by this parliament, and there is no reason in the world why all the activities of that board should not be discussed here. The . board itself, of course, is responsible to the government; in fact, the government can veto anything it wishes. I think it quite sufficient to say that the board will be under the control of the government and consequently under the control of this parliament, as will be seen if the committee considers the make-up of the board. Two of the members will be ministers of the crown, of whom one will be chairman. Three of the members will be civil servants, while the other three will be from the outside. I think the mere fact that the board will include two ministers and three civil servants will indicate at least that the board will be pretty thoroughly under the control of parliament and the government, and of course the funds must be voted by parliament. Therefore, discussion of any phase of the work of the board can take place here.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
May we have the assurance of the minister that, when the bill is brought down, it will provide that parliament must

vote the necessary funds? In connection with the broadcasting commission, as I understand it, we are in the unfortunate position, so far as this parliament is concerned, that we have a completely autonomous body, separate and distinct. The Department of Transport collects the licence fees from the people and deducts what it considers the cost of collecting, turning the balance over to the board without the yea or nay of this parliament, so we have no say about the matter. I do not want parliament to be in a similar situation in connection with another body.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: There is no great similarity between the two cases.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
I think the advantages and benefits to be gained by the distribution of films of this kind are very much to be desired. Having in mind the work that is done to-day by the national research council and the aid it has given industry in one way and another, I would urge on the government that when this film board is set up, not only should it have in mind the benefits to be derived from the circulation of films of this kind but should look at the matter from the commercial point of view as well. If these films are properly and carefully made, I am sure a demand will develop for them, and I do not see why this should not become an enterprise which not only will spend government money but may return a considerable revenue to the country.
If one were to go to the city of London, England, he might see one, or two, or half a dozen of these places where only newsreels of one kind or another are shown. Many of the pictures shown there are of national interest. I do not see why the same thing cannot be developed in Canada. At this time pictures of one kind or another are brought from other places. I believe there is no reason why, if we develop good reels of national importance, they could not be leased to these companies in a commercial way.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Shall the resolution carry?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: No; I am just waiting for everybody else to finish, because there are a number of things I want to say.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
I listened with a good deal of interest while the minister recited to us the personnel of the proposed film board. He suggested that he would be chairman, and that another minister would be associated with him. There would be three civil servants and, as I understood it, perhaps a school teacher, a pressman and a business man, or three private citizens of some kind.

National Film Board.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: In that case I shall not be on the board.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: That was merely a suggestion.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: I was going to suggest that, after all, if we are going to produce films, the presence of a showman on the board is highly to be desired.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
No one has thought of the moving-picture man.
. Mr. MASSEY: The moving-picture business is a complicated one, and, with all due deference to hon. gentlemen opposite who occupy the treasury benches I see no one who has the ability of a P.T. Barnum or a Cecil B. deMille.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: That is a compliment.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: It seems to me that political ability and the ability to produce an excellent motion picture film are two entirely different matters. Accordingly, I heartily commend to the minister the idea that among the three private citizens he selects for his film board he go as far as possible to obtain showmen for those positions.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: I understood the minister to say that different departments of government were producing their own films. Surely that cannot be correct. Has the government, or any department of it, any facilities of any kind to produce motion picture films, other than through the motion picture bureau in the minister's department?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
My hon. friend must have misunderstood what I said. Perhaps I did not make myself clear. When I say that the various departments have in some instances produced their own films, I mean they have had their films produced on their own initiative. They have given power, perhaps, to private concerns and perhaps to our own film bureau, but there was no restriction or any injunction on the part of the government that they must produce their films in our own bureau. That now will be the case. Ordinarily every film desired by any department must, if it passes the scrutiny of the board, be produced in the government bureau, except if it is thought by the board it can be produced better in some other way. It may be quite necessary for the film board itself, in the case of a national film or in the interests of any one department, to use some producing medium other than our own bureau. I do not know about that. Generally speaking, it is hoped that we shall use our own
71492-105i
bureau as much as possible. That is only natural. But it is quite possible to go beyond that.
One hon. member made some observations with respect to our making a commercial proposition of the matter. That is not the intention of the government. As I said, it is to do our own work, and to do it as efficiently as possible. It is quite possible that when we produce good films we may receive certain revenues from them, but I may also say for the information of the committee that it is not the intention through this medium to enter into competition with private business.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: There is one other matter- and the minister may refuse to answer if he desires. The government has the motion picture bureau. The man at the head of it has been there for some time, I believe. Is it in contemplation that that man shall be the commissioner, or is it thought that some one is going to be brought in in addition to the man already there?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Perhaps I am wrong, but it would seem that the hon. member asks his question because of a certain statement made in that connection. A suggestion as to who might be commissioner appeared in the press a few days ago. I should like to say to the committee that no consideration whatever has been given so far as to who the commissioner should be. There was no ground for the publication of the article as it appeared in the press. I am quite frank when I say that any statement as to who he might be would be quite out of order, because no consideration whatever has as yet been given to the matter.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Mr. Chairman, I had in mind expressing several thoughts in connection with the resolution when I saw it on the order paper. Frankly, however, the minister's statement to-night has indicated to me that when I read the resolution I may have had a misconception of what was contemplated. Therefore, in the main I am going to withhold any opposition I may have or any contributions I may wish to make to the debate until the bill is in committee. It might be well, however, if at this time I indicated quite clearly to the minister the line of thought that is in my mind in connection with this proposal. There is nothing political in it; it is just an ordinary, everyday matter of business. It so happens that I think I know something about the motion picture business-at least I should. I was in it at one time, and after I became a lawyer-

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
This is not an application for a commissionership, is it?
National Film Board

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
No, not at all. Nothing could induce me to take the job. Since that time I have in my legal activities at different times represented many phases of the motion picture industry. This is what I have in mind: In every province there is a motion picture bureau which, generally speaking, is an adjunct of or is in some way connected with the board of censors of that province. In every province the object of the film bureau is to produce pictures advertising the products of that particular province. Their objective has always been alleged to be the distribution of that film.
The first question I am going to raise when the bill is in committee, is that this is a duplication of what is being done by the provinces throughout Canada. Unless the minister can satisfy me that the board is going to accomplish something that is not being accomplished by the respective provincial motion picture bureaux, then I am going to oppose the measure on the plain, pure and simple principle that it is just another case of duplication of public services, the cost of all of which will ultimately come out of the pockets of the taxpayers. In the provinces, in the main, it comes out of the motion picture industry, because it is taxed in that way.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: May I ask a question?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Yes.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Is the hon. member referring to the provincially operated picture bureaux in the various provinces?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Yes. Every province has what is known as a motion picture bureau. There is one in Ontario and another in Que-bes. I am not so sure about New Brunswick, but there is one in Nova Scotia and one in British Columbia.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: May I ask another question?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Yes.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
Is my hon. friend of the
opinion that when the dominion government desires to issue a film, it should go to a provincial organization to have the work done?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
Not at all. I suggest that it should go where on at least two occasions dominion government departments have gone. They went there because they found they could get a film produced much more economically by this private enterprise. I do not want to' be contentious because I know the minister is terribly sincere in connection with the affairs of his department. All I am doing to-night is to ask him to familiarize himself 
with the subject matter before the bill is presented, and to indicate the questions which I shall ask at that time.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
The hon. member is really
discussing the merits of private or public ownership.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
I do not want to go into
that field at all. Long ago, when this motion picture bureau was in its infancy, I questioned the wisdom of such a bureau. On one occasion at least, I made representations to the Minister of Trade and Commerce of the government of which I was a supporter. His views and mine did not coincide, but that is beside the point. I still hold to the same contention. I expect the minister to be able to deal with these questions when the bill is in committee, and I think it only fair to advise him ahead of time of what I am going to ask so that the necessary data and information may be available to him.
First, before I support this bill I want to be satisfied that there will be no duplication of provincial services. Should the dominion government want a film produced which could not or would not in the ordinary course of events be produced by a provincial motion picture bureau, I want to know why that could not be produced by calling for tenders from the two extremely efficient motion picture producing agencies. These companies put out news films and other films of a kind which this bureau would contemplate using.
Second, the minister has stated that the dominion motion picture bureau has the most efficient equipment. I ask the minister to satisfy himself on that point before the bill goes into committee. If they have the most efficient equipment, I should like the minister to inquire why within the last eighteen months when the wheat board, I think it was, wanted to produce a film they engaged a private company to do the work. I think it was the Associated Screen News of Montreal which was called in to take the sound effects and produce the sound record. Again I must say that I do not know whether my information is correct and I have not inquired into the situation, but I am told that this was done because that company had more efficient and up-to-date equipment for the purpose of recording sound. I am dubious that the present motion picture bureau has the latest and most-up-to-date equipment. If it has not, I warn the minister that he will have to spend thousands of dollars for the purchase of such equipment. It would be much more profitable to have any motion

National Film Board
pictures required made by the Associated Screen News or the other concern, the name of which I have forgotten.
The next matter I am going to speak about is this advisory board. The hon. member for Greenwood (Mr. Massey) has mentioned this. When the minister was speaking, it struck me as most amazing that in establishing a board for the purposes suggested, apparently no thought is being given to having as a member a practical motion picture man.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
Perhaps the commissioner
will have that qualification.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
Do not misunderstand me. I have no criticism to make of the gentleman who is at the head of the motion picture bureau; I cannot even recall his name for the moment. I have no criticism of any kind to offer; it is merely a thought that I have in mind. I do suggest to the minister that he should take some advice from people skilled in the motion picture business.
Some mention was made of distribution in theatres and making it a profitable enterprise. I think the hon. member for St. Paul's (Mr. Ross) dealt with that phase of the matter. Let me say to the minister that to the best of my knowledge, information and belief, no country in the world has ever been able to get a distribution of film on a revenue basis, that is, film which would be produced by a government motion picture bureau. It just cannot be done.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
That is not our primary
purpose.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: That has not been possible, either in Canada or in the United States.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Why?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
For the simple reason that motion picture film is distributed by organizations known as exchanges. These people distribute film all across Canada. The basis of distribution is to rent film to the owners of motion picture theatres for so much money. Naturally the owners of motion picture theatres want to rent only those films which will draw people into their theatres, which will attract people who will be willing to pay admissions at the box-office. I am afraid that the number of people who would pay to see a film about the growing of wheat, about the bottling of milk, about certain health matters and so on, would not be sufficient to pay the small weekly salary of the man who operated the motion picture machine. You simply cannot distribute this film on a commercial basis. I will admit that if you can connect up with the proper distribution agencies, they may be able to get a measure of distribution for you by sending this film
out as a filler to small theatres which can afford to pay only a small weekly sum for their films for the week, whether it be two or three changes a week.
Another problem enters into the question of distribution. It is important that there should not be confusion in this matter. One must not think of distributing film in motion picture theatres in the same terms as one would think of distributing film in schools, public halls and so forth for educational purposes. The same film cannot be distributed in both cases. The film used in the motion picture theatre is what is known as 35 mm. film. This type of film is highly inflammable and powerful light must be used in projecting it. The projection machines cost at least S700, and sound equipment and photo-electric cells cost much more money. Every province in Canada has the most rigid regulations as to the type of room which shall be used as an operating room for the projection of such film. The 35 mm. film can be distributed only to motion picture theatres.
When one comes to talk about halls and schools, one must consider another type of film. This is a non-inflammable film known as the 16 mm. film. It can be projected with the use of an ordinary electric bulb, and it creates no fire hazard. If one is going to distribute to both sources, one must make two films. As a matter of fact, until within the last two years there was not any organization in this country set up to distribute the safe film or the 16 mm. film. Now there is, so I think any thought of putting this on a commercial basis might just as well be disposed of now as any other time. You can never get a demand from motion picture theatres for this kind of film, and I do not think you can ever get a revenue.
I point these matters out to the minister because, when the bill comes up, I should like him to be prepared to deal with them; and I seriously suggest to him that in the meantime he inquire as to the actual necessity of having this film board for government films, of setting up this organization with eight members of a board of governors, or whatever you want to call it, with a commissioner superimposed on top of the organization which you already have, and which I am frank to say in my opinion is just another burden of debt on the taxpayer of this country, duplicated in a large measure at the present time by the provincial bureaux. In any event, I suggest to the minister, everything that can be accomplished at the present time by his motion picture bureau and by the set-up he proposes could be accomplished, by any department which felt that it needed a film for distribution to advertise some-

thing of Canada in foreign lands, by their simply going before the treasury board and satisfying it as to the necessity of an expenditure for the purpose, and then going out and calling for tenders for making that film, from the companies now in business in Canada.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
Who would initiate, for
example, a national film?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: What does the minister mean by "a national film?"

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: A film which might be of an educational nature intended for all the people of the whole country, and which would not touch the particular interests of any one department.	.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: All right. Such a national film, I would say, might be initiated by the minister of any department.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: But it would not be his particular business.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
Well, suppose it was not
his particular business; let me put it in this way. The Department of Trade and Commerce, for example, is charged, is it not, with extending the trade and commerce of the Dominion of Canada? All right. In order to advance the sale of Canadian goods, or something of that kind, in foreign countries, the department decides that the best way to do it is to have a motion picture film made. Then what on earth is to prevent the minister from calling for tenders from private enterprise, the motion picture companies, to manufacture a film, asking them to submit a scenario or what he proposes should be in it, and having received the prices, to go to the treasury board and say, "Here is the amount of money I propose to spend and here is the purpose I hope to accomplish"? If treasury board thinks it is a good idea, they authorize it; if they do not think it is a good idea, they do not. Might I in turn say to the minister, who initiates any national films now?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Nobody. That is just the point.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: Well, then, what has the national motion picture bureau been doing during these last seven or eight years, if they have not been supporting something of that kind in this country?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
It has been doing work for the various departments. It is a branch of the Department of Trade and Commerce; but the Department of Trade and Commerce has never thought that it was its particular

duty to produce films that had anything to do with any activity other than applies to its own department, namely the promotion of business and sales. There might be a cultural film that the film board might think was quite proper for dissemination throughout the whole of Canada. It is not the particular duty of the Department of Trade and Commerce to initiate a film of that kind. It would not be the duty of the Department of Natural Resources or the Department of Agriculture. Nevertheless it would be in the interests of the country that it should be done. Who is going to do it; who is going to initiate it, if not a body such as this, which has a national view as well as doing the work for the various departments? That is what is in my mind with regard to it.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: I am sorry, Mr. Chairman, but it does seem to me that if there existed a national necessity for a national film, there would be many people in Canada urging that it be produced; it occurs to me that there would be many ministers in any government who would be anxious that it should be produced, and it could be initiated by any minister and could be submitted to the treasury board or some similar body. I say with great frankness that I look upon this as just another one of these things that constantly increase expenditure and the burden of taxation in this country and cannot justify its existence. I am sorry if my view differs from that of the minister. I can be no fairer than to give him ample warning of what I have in my mind, and ask him to prepare his brief and submit it to the house when he brings down his bill.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: I am not objecting to it for a moment.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: I cannot do more than that. I feel we are just piling up another government organization on top of the tremendous number of organizations we already have.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: In connection with this board, I have urged that if they were going to set it up they should do it so that to a certain extent they would have something come out of it; it would be commercial. For instance, in connection with the coming visit to Canada of the king and queen, who is to have the rights of taking these pictures in various places? Can private enterprise, for instance, be sold the rights, or are our own government bureaux to take these pictures?

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext: The question has been considered, but I am not in a position to answer it to-night.

subtopic: REVIEW OF GOVERNMENT FILM ACTIVITIES- INTERDEPARTMENTAL COMMITTEE TO CENTRALIZE DISTRIBUTION
speechtext:
It seems to me highly to be desired that in connection with this board the

Questions
splendid service that Mr. Frank Badgley has given to the dominion motion picture bureau should be recognized in a distinct and specific way. I had the good fortune to be associated with Mr. Badgley some years ago in the matter of the production of a moving picture, and so had occasion first hand to judge of his abilities in this regard; and when the minister made the statement he did a few moments ago in regard to the equipment we have on hand here, I am sure he was referring not only to the physical equipment but to the personnel as well. We are to be congratulated I think, upon having such a man as Mr. Badgley, and I would earnestly urge the minister that in setting up this board full consideration be given to this phase of the question.

speechtext: There is a matter about which I wish to ask the minister. I was called out of the house while he was speaking, and he may have covered it. If so, I am sorry. As far as I am concerned I have nothing but the highest regard for Mr. Badgley and the motion picture bureau. I think they have done excellent work. It is eleven o'clock, and I think we might as well report progress because I have a few questions to ask.
